newsitem.title: UK: Brazil demand steady on sugar freight market.
newsitem.headline: Brazil demand steady on sugar freight market.

text.p: The sugar freight market saw a spate of fresh enquiry on Tuesday with Brazil still at the forefront as a quoted origin.
But shipbrokers said rates remained on the low side.

Shipments are already starting to tail off from south Brazil's key port of Santos and freight orders are expected to increase from north Brazil, where mills have already started to crush cane from the 1996/97 harvest.

Of Tuesday's reported fixtures, Mauritius Sugar Syndicate was said to have covered its recent order for 17,500/18,000 tonnes of bulk sugar on its usual Port Louis to London run at 14.25 stg, 50 pence lower than for the last similar fixture.
Shipment dates were end Sept/early Oct.
Brokers reported talk of Glencore fixing a spot 25,000-tonne bulk cargo from Santos to the Black Sea at a rate in the region of $27.50.

Czarnikow Rionda was open with two new bagged orders, for a prompt 12/14,000 tonnes from north Brazil to West Africa and 2,500 tonnes from Buenaventura to east or west coast Mexico for September dates.
Glencore was in the market for a spot 15,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Santos to Casablanca with Tunisia, Egyptian Med, Black Sea and Baltic options.
Fiji Sugar Marketing issued two new bulk sugar enquiries for 15/25 October.

The first was for 15,000 tonnes from Fiji to Port Kelang, which shipbrokers said would achieve a rate in the low $20 bracket, and another for 19,000 tonnes to London, expected to fetch a rate in the high $20s.
Booker quoted for 8/12,000 tonnes in bulk from Georgetown to UK/Nantes for prompt shipment dates.
